Under the sails of your own ship, which is built like a karve (Karvi), you‘ll lead a crew, trade with foreign cultures and plunder other lands. Strengthen the skills of your crew by upgrading your ship and hiring stronger warriors. Whether you wish to establish new trade routes to secure rare goods or battle distant settlements to plunder their riches, your path to glory is yours to choose. But make sure to remember to stock up on beer and bread, so you have enough supplies to outmaneuver the competing clans. Successful planning will make you renowned throughout the lands, and secure your place in Norse legend as a fearless Jarl. Number of players: 2 - 4 Game duration: 90 mn Complexity: 4 / 5 Play Karvi and 1414 other games online. No download necessary - play directly from your web browser. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 THEME AND GOAL: 2 PRE-GAME: 3 PLAYER ORDER AND TURNS: 4 FREE ACTIONS: 5 MOVING YOUR SHIP: 6 MAIN ACTIONS: 7 END OF THE GAME THEME AND GOAL: Use your viking-dice to perform actions on the action rondel. Also use your scout ship (Karvi) to build colonies and gain Trade- and Raid-objective-tiles which may be activated later for points and other benefits. Upgrade your ships, build runestones, use cards and collect income during 3 rounds (4 rounds in 4p-game). The player with the most points (purple hex-symbols) will be the winner. PRE-GAME: Before you start the game: choose one of the three runestones from top-right of your playerboard as a free runestone. This is an objective tile that may give you end-game victory points if the easy or difficult goal is met. For the runestone chosen at the start of the game you do not need to fulfill the requirement on the bottom half. You may be able to build the remaining two runestones as an upgrade action during the game. You will then draw a starting card and automatically get starting resources based on this card. PLAYER ORDER AND TURNS: Turn order is determined by the action-rondel track. The next player is always the player whose dice is furthest behind on the track. Hence, it could be the same player several turns in a row. On your turn: 1. You may do free actions 2. You must move your active dice (the one furthest back) 3. You may do free actions When moving the die, you can move any number if spots, but only in a clockwise direction. The die can be placed on any free spot as long as you can pay the beer cost of the action-spot with beer (pips) from your active dice. The exception is the stop area (top left of the action rondel) where each dice will have to stop once, and can take only one of the six actions on the stop-tile each round. Once all players have stopped on the stop tile, next round begins. After placing the dice, immediately do the associated action. FREE ACTIONS: As many times as you’d like you may pay one gold to gain either one beer (pip), one provision on your ship, one silver-resource or one fur-resource. You may play any number of cards from your hand. Pay the cost on the top and gain the bottom half effect. If there are two separate bottom half effects you choose one of them. You may discard two cards from your hand to gain one gold. Once per turn (either before or after moving the dice) you may also move your ship: MOVING YOUR SHIP: You may move any number of spaces, but will have to pay one provision for each step you move. There may only be one ship on each spot. You may push another player’s ship away if you have more strength than that player, or by paying one provision to the bank. You will then interact with the spot you stop on: If this is a red raid-tile or yellow trade tile you may scout/choose one of these objective-tiles. You pay nothing when taking a tile. The back of the tile indicate the trade-cost range or strength-requirement, but this is only relevant when activating the tile from the action-rondel later, see below If the spot is a colony (house or tower) you may build that type of colony for free if you have one available. Immediately gain the points as indicated. Note that you may only interact with each space on the board one time e

[Rating: 3/10] played at PAXU. felt undercooked tbh. Maybe it was an issue with the english rulebook being inadequate in its current state. We had to reference the mediocre rulebook almost every time we drew a new card. The Iconography in this game is genuinely terrible.

[Rating: 3/10] What I dislike: - Uninspired, boring resource conversion game with 1001 symbols, effects, player powers, etc. - Rondel is interesting but in practice one keeps on waiting on other players turn to finish. - No meaningful interaction.

[Rating: 3/10] This is not a 4p game. Do not, under any circumstance agree to play this at 4p. I mean you can, just know it's probably more than a 3hour game. I never thought I'd see such an unbalanced Euro, and I appreciate Terminus (a entirely crappy game) even more than this. You can get continuously locked out of beer and provisions, which greatly limits your actions. Get ready to watch everyone else take multiple turns with ample resources while you twiddle your thumbs. I dont know why I haven't come across another game whose design commits such atrocities. At least Munchkin is meant to be random. Oh ye

[Rating: 5/10] Man, Hans im Glück was such a great game-crafting machine back in the day, but in the last few years they didn't put out anything great.  Same is true for this one which really is a perfectly mediocre game. There's nothing new, the artwork looks like it's from the past, the ships and their meat rings look bad and the gameplay isn't exciting at all.  It reminds me of "Raiders of the North Sea", but even more mediocre.

[Rating: 5/10] Sailing around the board, collecting rations to fuel your movement. There are some things going on but overall the game felt very stale to me.

[Rating: 5/10] I was underwhelmed by the gameplay. While the action selection rondel is one of my favorite mechanisms and I also like the idea of having to pay for the action space to choose, the eventual actions on the board and with the cards fell flat for me and felt highly repetitive. Over the course of the four rounds you would always be doing the same, just more of it - thats at least how the game felt to me.
